lines.text: I’m Parbat Lama, and my story starts here, in Sarlahi, on the plains of Nepal’s Terai.
This is where I did my basic schooling: a schoolboy from the Terai, with a long road ahead.
Walk with me. The road climbs north from here, all the way to the Himalaya.
In 2019 I moved to Kathmandu for my +2 at Uniglobe SS / College in Kamaladi.
I studied Management with Computer Science as my major, from January 2019 to December 2020.
College buses, a futsal ground, a basketball court, and my very first Computer Science classes.
In February 2021 I began a BSc (Hons) in Information Technology at Herald College Kathmandu.
It ran until October 2023, and it shaped everything that came after.
Less than a year in, I was already working as a developer alongside my studies.
January 2022 brought my first role in tech: Frontend Developer at Princelab, working remotely.
I built interfaces in Next.js, TypeScript and Tailwind.
A short, focused stint until July 2022: I shipped fast, and learned faster.
In June 2022 I joined PortPro in Lalitpur. Today I’m a Senior Full-Stack Engineer there.
We build drayOS, a logistics TMS for container drayage: trucking containers between ports, rail yards and warehouses.
On the front end: performance work, live maps in Mapbox GL and React Leaflet, and a shared design system.
Behind it, Node with Express and Hapi, MongoDB and Sequelize, real-time Socket.io and Pusher, and AWS CI/CD.
My component design system cut the lead time for new screens by about 40%.
In 2023 I received the AAA Scholarship at Herald College.
I earned it in my final year, while working at PortPro and finishing my degree.
Work showed me what to learn. The degree showed me how.
October 2023: I graduated with a BSc (Hons) in Information Technology from Herald College.
First Class Honours, the top classification, earned while shipping production code at PortPro.
Graduation ended a course. It didn’t end the learning.
In 2024 the AAA Scholarship came my way a second time.
Two years running: consistency, not luck.
And soon, it was time to give some of it back.
From August 2025 to April 2026, I went back to Herald as a Final Year Project Supervisor.
I guided about 12 student teams through their final-year projects.
Blockchain voting, AI recommendation engines for medicine, logistics and mental health, and full-stack platforms.
Now I’m building an orchestrator AI agent at PortPro.
It supervises dispatcher, billing and CSR sub-agents: it hands each one its task, and checks the result.
From a schoolboy in the Terai to software that coordinates other AI.
Over four years of shipping production software, and the next summit is already in view.
Away from the keyboard I trek, ride and take photographs. The dream is Everest.
Right now, I’m open to senior and contract roles.
Open my résumé, or just say hello. I’d love to hear what you’re building.
Chitwan National Park, in the Inner Terai: sal forest, tall grass and slow rivers.
Home to the one-horned rhino, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.
From here, the road leaves the plains and climbs into the hills.
Lumbini, in Rupandehi: the birthplace of the Buddha.
The Maya Devi Temple marks the spot, beside the sacred pool and the Ashoka Pillar.
Monasteries built by many countries line the long canal of the Monastic Zone.
Phewa Lake in Pokhara, under Machhapuchhre, the Fishtail mountain.
On still days the peaks show in the water, and the boats rest on the shore.
Paragliders launch from Sarangkot, on the ridge above the lake.
Rani Pokhari, the Queen’s Pond, in the heart of Kathmandu.
King Pratap Malla built it in 1670, with a small temple at its centre.
Swayambhunath, on its hill west of the city.
The stupa’s painted eyes look out over the whole Kathmandu Valley.
Kathmandu Durbar Square, at Basantapur: the old royal palace and its temples.
Pagoda roofs and carved windows, centuries of Newar craft.
